reasons.G: The clearest road read of the run with a dark, matte loam and a violet far rim and light that belong to no other area.
reasons.H: Its inverted value plan, pale bone ground under a dark trodden road, is instantly its own place and reads from every camera.
reasons.A: Plum-brown terraces under violet slate with a wine accent are distinct and moody, needing only a lighter road.
reasons.C: Warm rust spoil against a cool track with verdigris is a clear copper-mine identity with a good hue split.
reasons.F: The turquoise shrine-tile accent on warm ground is a strong idea worth an area once the clay is made redder.
reasons.D: The best of the green cluster: pale limestone and a clear road, and it becomes the marsh once its water role exists.

fixes.G: walk ground 5 values darker and slightly more umber
fixes.H: walk sand cooled and desaturated toward grey-white bone, same value
fixes.A: road cobblestone about 12 values lighter and cooler
fixes.C: far slate shifted to cool slag grey; walk ground 6 values darker
fixes.F: walk sand and rocks redder, road 10 values lighter
fixes.D: walk mud darker and greener-black, accent warmer amber; add the green-black water surface role

notes: B and E were dropped: both render as the same mid-olive field as D and the moor, and lose their named idea (snow, near-black peat). Palettes that differ by value plan, not just hue, survive night best; descriptions promising 'near-black' or 'snow' should be checked against swatch value, and a water-surface role is the most requested missing piece.
